title: Interface With Whom? Markov Blanket Claims Depend on the Observation Protocol (with the technical note "Finite-Window Path Screening in Linear Diffusions: An Exact Condition and a Residual-Leak Formula")
description: We build on the free energy principle (FEP), which describes a Markov blanket as the interface between inside and outside. We offer one more point of view: an interface is always an interface with someone, so a blanket claim is complete only when the observation protocol is stated. For linear stochastic systems we give exact results. (1) On a finite window, internal and external paths are conditionally independent given the blanket path iff there is no direct inside-outside coupling and M = A_BI^T D_B^-1 A_BE = 0, with a start condition; with a long history the start condition drops out, and a causal reader of the past blanket needs the same M = 0. (2) For a stationary reader of the whole time line, a spectral form of this condition is known (Fasen-Hartmann & Schenk, 2025); a graphical d-separation form for SDE sample paths (Boeken & Mooij, 2026) gives the sufficiency direction; there, unlike on a finite window, the wiring cut is not necessary. (3) Screening and encoding (the FEP's synchronisation map) need different conditions. (4) The residual leak when M != 0 has an exact Riccati formula. We give a single-file tool, all scripts, a real-data case on fMRI that remains undecided, and a list of failed predictions. The point of view comes from a wider framework we are developing (IFO); every result holds without it.
notes: Version 1.0.1 adds the comparison with Boeken & Mooij (2026), causal graphs for SDEs; no result changes. Version 1.0: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23524009.
